sentences.en: Today, a Biden victory was expected to translate into Democratic control of the Senate.

sentences.zh: 朱莉·戴维斯将解释为什么这种情况没有发生，以及两党如何为佐治亚州的双参议员选举做准备，这两场选举将决定华盛顿的权力平衡。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, November 11th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月11日，星期三。

sentences.en: Julie, until now, we have been very focused, I think understandably, on the presidential race.
sentences.zh: 朱莉，到目前为止，我们一直非常关注——我认为这是可以理解的——总统大选。

sentences.en: But now that that race has been called and called for President-elect Joe
sentences.zh: 但现在这场选举已经有了结果，并宣布当选总统为乔·

sentences.en: Biden, we want to turn to the fate of Congress, which, alas, is not at all a settled matter.

sentences.en: So just how unsettled a matter is Congress at this moment?
sentences.zh: 那么此刻国会的悬念究竟有多大？

sentences.en: Well, it's still pretty unsettled.
sentences.zh: 嗯，悬念依然很大。

sentences.en: Democrats are on track to have held their House majority.
sentences.zh: 民主党人有望保住他们在众议院的多数席位。

sentences.en: They had kind of a rougher night than they expected, and they lost some seats in the House.
sentences.zh: 他们的处境比预期的要艰难一些，并且在众议院失去了一些席位。

sentences.en: But in the Senate, it's a much more complicated picture, and majority still hangs in the balance.
sentences.zh: 但在参议院，情况要复杂得多，多数席位仍然悬而未决。

sentences.en: So let's talk about how we get to this moment.
sentences.zh: 让我们来谈谈我们是如何走到这一步的。

sentences.en: What Senate races were on the ballot on election day, last Tuesday?
sentences.zh: 在上周二的选举日，选票上有哪些参议院竞选？

sentences.en: So going into this election, you know, Republicans had a lot more to lose than Democrats did.
sentences.zh: 所以在这次选举前，你知道的，共和党人比民主党人有更多的东西要输。

sentences.en: They had
sentences.zh: 他们有

sentences.en: 23 seats they were defending.
sentences.zh: 23个席位需要捍卫。

sentences.en: Democrats, because of the way Senate races are staggered every two years, only were defending 12 seats.
sentences.zh: 由于参议院每两年交错改选一次的机制，民主党人只需捍卫12个席位。

sentences.en: And they had some pretty good pickup opportunities around the country.
sentences.zh: 并且他们在全国各地有一些相当不错的翻盘机会。

sentences.en: You had senators who were facing voters in Colorado, Cory Gardner, Martha McSally in Arizona.
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多州的参议员面临选民的考验，科里·加德纳，亚利桑那州的玛莎·麦克萨利。

sentences.en: They were both very vulnerable and seen as, you know, potentially going to lose.
sentences.zh: 他们都非常脆弱，被认为，你知道的，有可能落败。

sentences.en: You had Susan Collins in Maine, who, you know, is a moderate.
sentences.zh: 缅因州的苏珊·柯林斯，你知道的，是一个温和派。

sentences.en: President Trump is very unpopular in her state.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统在她的州非常不受欢迎。

sentences.en: So she was seen as very vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 因此她被认为非常脆弱。

sentences.en: Tom Tillis in North Carolina was also seen as somebody who could, you know, potentially lose his seat to a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 北卡罗来纳州的汤姆·蒂利斯也被视为有可能在席位竞选中输给民主党人的人。

sentences.en: But Democrats also knew they were going into the cycle with at least one member who was almost certain to lose.
sentences.zh: 但民主党人也知道，他们在进入这一选举周期时，至少有一名成员几乎注定要落败。

sentences.en: That's Doug Jones in Alabama.
sentences.zh: 那就是阿拉巴马州的道格·琼斯。

sentences.en: So given that the Senate balance of power is very narrow, Democrats have 47 seats, Republicans have
sentences.zh: 因此，鉴于参议院的权力平衡非常微弱，民主党有47个席位，共和党有

sentences.en: 53, they were going to have to pick up at least four seats in order to be able to have a chance at control of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 53个，他们必须至少赢得四个席位，才能有机会控制参议院。

sentences.en: And even then, that would only be the case if Joe Biden were to win the presidency.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，这也只有在乔·拜登赢得总统宝座的情况下才成立。

sentences.en: Therefore, his vice president would have the power to cast tie-breaking votes.
sentences.zh: 因此，他的副总统将拥有投出打破平局关键一票的权力。

sentences.en: So the math was full of opportunities for Democrats, but it was still going to be an uphill battle.
sentences.zh: 所以对民主党来说，数字充满了机遇，但这仍然会是一场艰难的战斗。

sentences.en: And that's kind of how they were looking going into Election Day.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们进入选举日时的看法。

sentences.en: And as the months went on and President Trump's popularity sagged even more, the pandemic got worse.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，特朗普总统的支持率进一步下滑，大流行变得更加严重。

sentences.en: The economy was getting worse.

sentences.en: The polls were showing that voters were extremely unhappy with Republican leadership in Washington.
sentences.zh: 民意调查显示，选民对华盛顿的共和党领导层极其不满。

sentences.en: Texas, where John Cornyn was up for re-election.

sentences.zh: 甚至南卡罗来纳州，林赛·

sentences.en: So by Election Day, they had pretty high hopes of doing very well in competitive states and maybe even being able to flip some of these
sentences.zh: 因此，到了选举日，他们对在竞争激烈的州取得好成绩抱有很高的期望，甚至可能在一些他们过去没有机会的

sentences.en: redder states where they haven't had opportunities in the paSt. And then the air starts to come out of the balloon.

sentences.en: That's right.

sentences.zh: 在亚利桑那州，曾与前国会议员结婚的宇航员马克·凯利

sentences.zh: 加布里埃尔·吉福兹成功击败了玛莎·麦克萨利，这位共和党人此前曾被任命为

sentences.zh: 而在科罗拉多州这个日益倾向民主党的州，前州长约翰·希肯洛珀以压倒性优势击败了

sentences.en: And he was running kind of on his character and as a wholesome, you know, better candidate than Tom

sentences.en: Tillis.

sentences.en: And so far, if there's a theme here, it seems to be if President Trump did really well in the state, then the Republican incumbent did pretty well in the state.

sentences.en: But Susan Collins, veteran, moderate Republican, she's the last remaining New England Republican in Congress, was able to win re-election.
